name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.95.0 — the journey review page (brief 22a): `stop open journey:<j>` now points at `/review/<j>.html`, a derived three-pane page (screens rail, per-screen artboards with `happy|empty|loading|error` state tabs at `?state=<s>` on the served mock, and a question/note inspector answered in place with `J K Y N Esc \`) built by the new `lib/review-page.js`/`lib/review.browser.js` and routed through `design-atlas.js`; the approve control mirrors the on-disk gate, disabled while any question or note is open; `shapes`/`theme`/`signoff`/`variants:<j>` stops keep the atlas URL. Plugin chrome (atlas, review page, galleries, notes layer) is now one doctrine home, design.md § Design Canon, authored under the frontend-design skill in the shadcn idiom on viewer.css's register. Fixes the atlas's frame-height floor: a viewport-filling mock (`100vh` app shells, sign-in screens) measured its `scrollHeight` before the iframe reached its declared height and rendered as a squashed ~150px strip; every card and artboard iframe now carries `width`+`height` from the primary viewport before measurement. 7.94.0 — questions on the wireframe (brief 22a): every inferred/invented product assumption the session writes while drawing a journey is pinned as a question (`ledger add … --screen <label>`, or `ledger ask --id <rowId> --screen <label>`) on the screen it belongs to; the served page answers it (`Yes, that's right` / `No, it's…` + text / `Later`), the answer writes the ledger row's status (`confirmed`/`overridden` + date, via new `POST /__notes/answer`) before resolving the note, and `journey-approved`/`variant-picked`/`approved` refuse while a question is unanswered, naming the ledger ids first; free-form notes gain an optional `reason` (missing-screen · wrong-direction · wrong-words · other) and the mock-page composer gains a scope toggle; `notes open` prints an open-questions block first and `ledger counts` gains a derived catch-provenance line (`question · note · unlinked`, from `addressed.ledgerRow`) — no new ledger column. 7.93.0 — mocks ends at wireframes (ADR-0008 amending ADR-0006, brief 22a): `/spec:mocks`'s chain drops `SKIN` and `REVIEW`, gains `SIGNOFF` (`SEED → SHAPES → WIREFRAMES → THEME → SIGNOFF → APPROVED`); `direction-composed` recomposes the seed's dense screen per direction (a second at most, never a full-product skin); `--mark approved` stamps every top-level mock `data-status="approved"` itself and records the sign-off stop's own decider — `--decider` is a retired flag; a host checkpointed mid-SKIN or mid-REVIEW derives THEME or SIGNOFF from its existing marks on the next run, nothing on disk is deleted, and ledger rows written under the retired step names keep parsing.
